<0>Accordion and Toggle Group values are always arrays.</0> Even in single mode, `value="a"` becomes `value={["a"]}`. Tabs keep a single value.
<0>Anchored popups gain a `Positioner`.</0> Menu, Select, Popover and Tooltip go from <l1/> to <l2/>. Dialog has no Positioner; it uses `Backdrop` and `Popup`.
<0>Can I mix Radix and Base UI components in one project?</0> Yes. You carry both dependencies while you migrate. Many projects will stay mixed for a long time and that is fine.

<0>Checkbox and radio menu items keep the menu open.</0> `closeOnClick` defaults to `false` for `CheckboxItem` and `RadioItem`. Plain items still close. This is arguably the better default, but it is a change your users will notice.
<0>Dialog and Alert Dialog.</0> Learn the `Backdrop` and `Popup` structure and the `details.cancel()` pattern here, where there is no Positioner to confuse things.
<0>Do I need to change my theme tokens?</0> No. `--background`, `--primary`, `--radius` and the rest are unchanged. The primitive layer is independent of the Tailwind side.
<0>Does Base UI support React Server Components?</0> Base UI primitives are client components, the same as Radix. Keep the `"use client"` directive where shadcn/ui puts it.
<0>Is Radix deprecated?</0> No. shadcn/ui ships every component for both libraries, and the team still runs Radix in production.
<0>Leaf components with no popup</0>: Switch, Checkbox, Slider, Toggle, Progress. Mostly rename work.

<0>Navigation menus open faster.</0> Base UI's hover `delay` defaults to 50ms. Radix's `delayDuration` defaulted to 200ms. Fast menus feel great until someone sweeps their mouse across the header and three panels fire in a row. Tune it.

<0>Open-state selectors change.</0> `data-[state=open]:` variants become `data-open:`. This one hides in your `className` strings and in `cva` variants, so grep for `data-[state=` before you call the migration done.
<0>Popover and Tooltip.</0> Add the `Positioner`.
<0>Select values are nullable.</0> A controlled Select holds `Value | null`, not `string`. Your <l2/> becomes <l3/>, and every place that read the value as a string needs a guard.
<0>Select, Combobox, Dropdown Menu, Context Menu.</0> Nullable values, `closeOnClick`, and the whole popup tree. Do these last, with the most tests.

<0>Tabs activate manually by default.</0> In Radix, arrow keys move focus and activate the tab. In Base UI, arrow keys move focus and you press Enter or Space to activate. If your tests or users expect the Radix behavior, set `activateOnFocus` on the list.
<0>Tabs and Accordion.</0> Fix the array values and decide on `activateOnFocus`.
<0>Where is the official change log?</0> The July 2026 entry is at <1>ui.shadcn.com/docs/changelog/2026-07-base-ui-default</1>.
<0>`Overlay` is now `Backdrop`.</0> Rename and move on.
<0>`asChild` becomes `render`.</0> This is the one everyone meets first.

<0>`onOpenChange` has a second argument.</0> Radix lets you call `event.preventDefault()` to stop a close. Base UI passes `(open, details)` and you call `details.cancel()`. The `details.reason` field tells you whether it was the Escape key, an outside press or something else, which is handy for "unsaved changes" dialogs.

I maintain <0>HextaUI</0>, a shadcn/ui registry built on Base UI, so I have spent most of this year inside both primitive layers. This is the guide I wished existed in July: what changed, what did not, every API difference you will hit, and the order to migrate in if you decide to.
I would also not switch primitive layers and redesign the components in the same PR. The point of shadcn/ui is that you own the code. Owning it means reading the diff.

I would not run a codemod across the whole tree and hope. The build-breaking changes are easy to find. The silent ones are not, and a codemod cannot tell you that your settings page now needs two keystrokes to switch tabs.

Should you migrate an existing app?
Silent behavior changes
Stay on Radix if the app is stable, you are not blocked on a missing primitive, and nobody on the team has a specific complaint. Nothing you depend on is going away.
The `render` prop takes an element or a function. The function form gives you the state, which is useful for things like a trigger that changes its icon when open.
Then `git diff components/ui/dialog.tsx` and read every line before you keep it.

Two reasons were given. Base UI had reached a stable 1.6.0 with over six million weekly downloads, and projects created through `shadcn/create` were already choosing Base UI over Radix about two to one. The default followed what people were picking.
